_readme: Deploy-time models file of AI Prism (docs/onboarding-deployment.md, section Models file). Edit this file, or edit a copy and run ./deploy.sh --models-file my-models.json <PROFILE> (deploy.ps1: -ModelsFile my-models.json).

models: the chat models of the picker, IN THIS ORDER (the first is the default of new chats). Each item: id (AI Gateway endpoint), label, and optionally blurb, priceIn and priceOut (USD per 1M tokens). A price left out follows the curated list price; a blurb left out keeps the curated, translated one.

The app applies this file on the first admin request after a deploy that CHANGED it: it enables the listed models (name, order, price) and disables the other chat models. Edits made in the admin Models tab last until the file changes again. A catalog an admin already curated is only extended the first time (nothing is switched off).
Workspace without OpenAI, Google or open models? Delete those lines from models.

imageModels: the image generation models, IN THE PICKER'S ORDER (the first is the default). Each item is one of two kinds: {id, label, blurb} a serving endpoint, or {provider, model, label, blurb} a target of a Unity Catalog Model Provider Service (provider = catalog.schema.service), called through the AI Gateway native Gemini API with the user's token.

Provider example: {"provider": "my_catalog.my_schema.gemini_models", "model": "gemini-3-pro-image", "label": "Nano Banana Pro"}. Users need USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA and EXECUTE ON MODEL PROVIDER SERVICE. List the allowed targets: databricks ai-gateway get-model-provider-service model-provider-services/<provider> -p <PROFILE>.

Both kinds can share the list; an item with "id" and "provider"/"model" together is refused. "imageModels": [] turns image generation off; without the key the app keeps its default (Nano Banana 2 as a serving endpoint) and the image models enabled in the admin tab.

The deploy validates this file before writing anything (node scripts/validate-models-config.mjs models.json --profile <PROFILE>) and checks each image model in the workspace. Technical flags (tools, vision, temperature, reasoning) live in server/llm.ts; an id outside that list works with conservative defaults.
